article_title: EU Fines AliExpress a Record €550 Million Over Unsafe and Counterfeit Goods Under the Digital Services Act
summary: Submission approvable with 1 minor warning(s) — file a corrections record on merge

findings.message: Claim misattributed to the wrong cited outlet
findings.details: Body states: 'Euronews also reported that the Commission found AliExpress had underestimated the gap between its available human moderators and the scale of the workload, and had not adequately assessed how its recommender and advertising systems exacerbate the spread of illegal products.' The moderator/workload clause is confirmed in the Euronews snapshot ('underestimating the gap between the number of human moderators available and the scale of their workload'), but the 'recommender and advertising systems' clause does not appear anywhere in the Euronews snapshot (source-2.html.gz) — it is a close paraphrase of a sentence in The Register's snapshot instead ('did not conduct an adequate assessment of how its recommender and advertising systems exacerbate the spread of illegal products', source-1.html.gz). The fact itself is true and sourced, just to the wrong outlet.

findings.message: Currency mismatch on a cited figure
findings.details: Body states 'X (€120 million)' citing ABC News as the source for the prior DSA fine comparison. The ABC News/AP snapshot (source-3.html.gz) states the X fine was '$120 million' (USD), not €120 million. The Temu figure in the same sentence (€200 million) is correctly denominated per the same snapshot ('Temu, was fined 200 million euros'). This is a subordinate comparative figure in the Analysis section, not part of the headline/summary/lead.

content_preview.title: EU Fines AliExpress a Record €550 Million Over Unsafe and Counterfeit Goods Under the Digital Services Act
content_preview.summary: The European Commission fined AliExpress €550 million for Digital Services Act failures tied to counterfeit and unsafe products, the largest DSA penalty issued so far.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The European Commission has fined AliExpress €550 million for breaching the Digital Services Act (DSA), according to the [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-fines-aliexpress-eu550-million-breaching-digital-services-act). The penalty, announced on July 20, 2026, is [the largest ever fine issued under the Digital Services Act](https://www.theregister.com/legal/2026/07/21/europe-slaps-aliexpress-with-550-million-fine-for-selling-dodgy-goods/52...

recommendations: Before merging, the human reviewer should write a corrections file at src/content/corrections/<YYYY-MM>/<article-slug>.json documenting the warning(s).
Consider adding trusted domains to config/source_allowlist.txt

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean News-category structure (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis), 636 words (within the 400-1200 range for News). Prose is clear, factual, and well-organized. The Analysis section is clearly labeled and appropriately contextualizes the fine within a pattern of DSA enforcement rather than smuggling in unsourced opinion.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200) by chief:review and their gzip snapshots were read in full from disk at sources/2026-07/eu-fines-aliexpress-a-record-550-million-over-unsafe-and-counterfeit-goods-under-the-digital-services-act/. I independently recomputed the sha256 of each decompressed file and confirmed all four match the manifest.json values exactly (no substitution/tampering). Per-source verification: (1) source-0.html.gz — European Commission press release (digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu). Confirms the €550M fine, DSA breach, 20 July 2026 publication date, and the full Henna Virkkunen quote verbatim including her title 'Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy.' (2) source-1.html.gz — The Register (Simon Sharwood, published Tue 21 Jul 2026). Confirms 'the largest ever fine issued under the Digital Services Act,' the four-part list of Commission findings (detection system, penalty enforcement, mis-categorisation loophole, counterfeit prevention), the 'six percent of global turnover' / '$148 billion' / 'March 31st' figures, the 'mitigating circumstances... novelty of the Digital Services Act' quote, and the ~$9 billion theoretical-maximum framing — all verbatim or accurately paraphrased. This snapshot is also the true source of the 'recommender and advertising systems' finding that the article mistakenly attributes to Euronews (see Attribution finding). (3) source-2.html.gz — Euronews (Vincenzo Genovese, published 20/07/2026). Confirms the 2024 proceedings start date, the October 20, 2026 corrective-action-plan deadline and two-month decision window, the brand-authorization system finding, the human-moderator/workload gap finding, and the full AliExpress statement quote verbatim ('We disagree with today's decision... considering all available options'). Grep-confirmed that the words 'recommender' and 'advertising system' do NOT appear anywhere in this snapshot, which is the basis for the Attribution finding above. (4) source-3.html.gz — ABC News / AP wire (Mike Corder, published July 20, 2026, 7:54 AM). Confirms the June 2025 preliminary-ruling conduct cutoff, the Virkkunen quote (verbatim, second independent confirmation), the AliExpress statement (verbatim, second independent confirmation), and the prior-fines comparison — but the snapshot states the X fine as '$120 million' (USD), while the article's body text renders it as '€120 million,' which is the basis for the Factual Accuracy finding above. No snapshot fetch failures occurred; no WebFetch fallback was needed for any source — all four reads were from the committed disk snapshots.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline, summary, and lead (Overview paragraph) are each fully supported by the primary source (European Commission) and independently corroborated by The Register, Euronews, and ABC News/AP. Every direct quotation in the article (Virkkunen's statement, AliExpress's statement, the Register's 'mitigating circumstances' and 'six percent of global turnover' quotes) was checked character-by-character against the snapshots and reproduces verbatim. Two subordinate specifics do not hold up on close inspection: (1) a claim attributed to Euronews about recommender/advertising systems actually originates in The Register's reporting, not Euronews's; (2) the X fine is rendered as €120 million in the article but the cited ABC News source states $120 million (a currency, not just rounding, discrepancy). Both are single, isolated, subordinate-claim errors in the body (not the headline/summary/lead) and are each honestly correctable with one corrections entry.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Direct quotes are properly bracketed and attributed with in-line source links.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior coverage of AliExpress or this DSA action; none found. One related article exists (src/content/articles/2026-07/15-eu-commission-finds-instagram-and-facebooks-addictive-design-breaches-digital-services-act.md) but it concerns a separate, still-preliminary DSA finding against Meta/Instagram/Facebook over addictive design — a different company, different alleged violation, and different enforcement stage (no fine yet). This AliExpress submission is a genuinely new, distinct story with its own primary source and its own imposed fine; not a duplicate or rewrite of existing coverage.
editor_notes.human_requested: human_requested is false in the submission; standard scrutiny applied (which independently included full-snapshot verification of every source, exceeding the baseline requirement).
editor_notes.source_allowlist: 3 of 4 domains (digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu, theregister.com, euronews.com) are explicitly present in config/source_allowlist.txt. The 4th, abcnews.com, is not literally listed — only abcnews.go.com is. I checked whether abcnews.com is a redirect/alias of the listed domain: curl -I against the live URL returned HTTP 200 directly on abcnews.com (no redirect to abcnews.go.com; cookies are set with Domain=abcnews.com), and the snapshot content is genuine ABC News/AP wire content (byline 'By MIKE CORDER Associated Press', footer '© 2026 ABC News', 'ABC News Network' branding). This reads as ABC News operating a second, shorter first-party domain for wire-story content rather than a distinct or disreputable outlet impersonating ABC News. I judge this a cosmetic allowlist gap, not a source-credibility problem, and recommend (per the script's own recommendation) adding abcnews.com to config/source_allowlist.txt going forward. It is not treated as a corrections-worthy issue since the outlet is genuine and the content is accurately cited.
concerns: A claim about AliExpress's recommender/advertising systems is attributed to Euronews in the body but is actually sourced from The Register's reporting, not Euronews's.
The article states the prior X DSA fine as €120 million, but the cited ABC News/AP source states $120 million (USD) — a currency discrepancy, not merely a rounding difference.
abcnews.com is not literally present in config/source_allowlist.txt (only abcnews.go.com is), though verification shows it is a genuine first-party ABC News domain, not a redirect or impersonation.
recommendations: File a corrections record with two entries: (1) correcting the Euronews/Register attribution mix-up on the recommender/advertising-systems finding, (2) correcting the X fine's currency from €120 million to $120 million (or clarifying it should be a converted/approximate euro figure if intended as such).
Add abcnews.com to config/source_allowlist.txt so future submissions citing ABC News's wire-story domain do not trip the allowlist check.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively solid, accurately headlined and well-sourced News piece on a genuinely new story. The core fine amount, date, regulatory rationale, and both direct quotes are verified verbatim against primary and wire sources. Two isolated, subordinate-claim errors (an outlet misattribution and a currency mismatch on a comparative figure) keep this from a clean APPROVE, but both are narrow, factual, and can be honestly and fully summarized in a short corrections record without gutting the article's lead. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
